title: operator upgrade hook race causing ephemeral secret exposure — immediate hotfix and preflight gate
creator: Asha Menon
description: Several on-prem customer escalations reported tenant failures during operator/Helm upgrades. Root cause: a race between post-upgrade helm hooks and the operator reconciliation loop that caused ephemeral secrets (used briefly during migration) to be written into a cluster-scoped namespace incorrectly, making them accessible to other controllers. This ticket drives an immediate hotfix to prevent further exposure, plus a durable preflight gating change to the upgrade path.
background: On 2026-03-09, three customers reported post-upgrade API auth failures and audit logs showing ephemeral secret objects persisted outside tenant namespaces. Investigation traced the issue to a late-running post-upgrade helm hook that created temp credentials while the operator simultaneously attempted a manifest merge; timing allowed the hook to create a Secret without the tenant namespace label. The cluster's admission controller did not block unlabeled secrets because the hook ran under the release serviceAccount. Prior incidents in the repo hinted at hook timeouts and manifest merge races but none resulted in secret leakage until now.
impact_summary: Affected customers experienced service errors (pod restarts and token auth failures) after upgrades. Although secrets were short-lived, the exposure window is unacceptable for regulated customers. Active escalations: 3 customers (two enterprise customers with VPC/on-prem installs, one dedicated tenant). Estimated blast radius: up to three tenant namespaces per cluster depending on timing.
reproduction_steps: Deploy staging onprem operator with helm release v3.4.0 and simulate long-running post-upgrade hook (sleep + create secret)
Trigger operator reconcile concurrently by toggling a CRD field to force manifest merge
Observe created Secret without tenant labels in kube-system or default namespace when reconciliation completes while hook is mid-flight
Verify admission logs show no mutation for the unlabeled secret because hook used release SA
proposed_solution: 1) Emergency hotfix that enforces a pre-hook validation and post-hook cleanup: helm chart will include a pre-upgrade hook that records an upgrade token in a release-scoped ConfigMap and a post-upgrade finalizer that verifies any created secrets have the tenant label and deletes any that do not. 2) Operator change: introduce an atomic manifest-merge operation where the operator holds a lightweight upgrade lock (leader-elect mutex per-tenant) while applying merged manifests to prevent concurrent hook-created objects from escaping tenant scoping. 3) Admission policy: add a fail-closed mutating webhook rule for unlabeled secrets created by known release serviceAccounts during upgrades. 4) Release: operator-3.4.1-hotfix with a staged rollout backported to the last two supported operator branches.
acceptance_criteria: Hotfix released and applied to two impacted customers without regression
No unlabeled secrets observed in post-upgrade audit during test runs
Operator tests demonstrate manifest-merge atomicity under concurrent hook execution
Admission rule denies creation of unlabeled secrets from release SAs in upgrade windows
Security review sign-off obtained and communicated to customers
rollout_plan: Build hotfix branch from operator main -> tag operator-3.4.1-hotfix
Create canary cluster in staging and run upgrade smoke-tests with artificial hook delays
If canary passes, contact Customer Success and schedule rolling hotfix for each affected customer during off-peak window
Apply hotfix to remaining onprem clusters in waves of 5 with monitoring windows
Monitor for failures for 48h per wave, escalate to on-call if errors exceed threshold
rollback_plan: If hotfix causes regressions, revert operator release to previous tag and restore operator configuration from pre-upgrade backups
For customer clusters with persistent issues, run surgical cleanup script to remove incorrectly labeled secrets and re-provision credentials using operator-managed flow
Open emergency rollback playbook to coordinate with SRE and CS for any clusters that need manual intervention
telemetry_and_alerts: Add alert: upgrade.unlabeled_secrets_detected > 0 for production clusters -> P0 pager
Dashboards: per-cluster upgrade health, leader-lock wait times, helm-hook durations
Audit logs: surface serviceAccount and createdBy fields for secrets created during upgrade windows
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for manifest-merge mutex and leader lock behavior
Integration test: orchestrate concurrent helm hook + operator reconcile and assert no unlabeled secrets
E2E: run upgrade on a copy of affected customer manifests with production-like load
Chaos test: introduce artificial hook delays and process restarts to validate atomicity
dependencies_notes: Admission webhook change requires infra RBAC update and will be coordinated with security and installer teams. Backporting requires release engineering sign-off.
